newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: ANALYSTS DOWNPLAY BOE, NORWICH STAKE TALK.
newsitem.headline: ANALYSTS DOWNPLAY BOE, NORWICH STAKE TALK.

text.p: Analysts on Thursday downplayed speculation that South African firm The Board of Executors Ltd (BOE) may have set its sights on taking a sizable stake in Norwich Holdings to secure a foothold in the insurance industry.

Business Report newspaper on Thursday quoted unnamed sources saying a complex transaction may be in the offing, whereby BOE may buy a stake in the insurer from the NBS Boland Bank group, which holds a 25 percent interest.
Terry Norton, the managing director of NBS Holdings, declined to comment.
Boland and BOE could not be reached for comment.

"I don't see why they would want to buy into Norwich...The (insurance) industry is in a material phase where you are not seeing real growth on the recurring premium side, although the single premium side is showing a bit of growth," said Dave Southey, an analyst at stockbroker Edey Rogers.
Another analyst who asked not be be identified said: "I cannot see them having the appetite to acquire the stake in Norwich. They are not big enough although they could raise the money."
The paper said BOE, a financial services firm which offers asset management and investment services to private and corporate clients, has long wanted to add an insurance arm to its portfolio.
It said BOE was understood to have been a contender for Protea Assurance's life business which was last year bought by Commercial Union of South Africa Ltd for 250 million rand.

Norwich on Monday issued a cautionary notice to say it was in talks. The paper said NBS Holdings and Boland Bank Ltd, which merged in December to create South Africa's fifth largest bank, were still covered by cautionaries.
